newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Diabetes rate on track to double by 2025, WHO says.
newsitem.headline: Diabetes rate on track to double by 2025, WHO says.

text.p: Diabetes, which affects 120 million people, will strike 250 million by the year 2025, due to an ageing population with poor eating habits and a sedentary lifestyle, the World Health Organisation (WHO) said on Thursday.

But insulin, an essential drug to keep the chronic, hereditary disease in check, remains unavailable or unaffordable in some developing countries, especially in Africa, according to the United Nations agency.
The Geneva-based WHO issued the statement on the occasion of the sixth annual World Diabetes Day, being observed on Thursday.
"Recently compiled data show that approximately 120 million people suffer from diabetes mellitus worldwide, and that this number will rise to over 250 million by the year 2025," it said.
"This more than twofold rise is projected to occur because of populating ageing, unhealthy diets, obesity and a sedentary lifestyle," it added.

Diabetes mellitus -- whose complications include blindness, kidney failure, heart attacks and amputation of the limbs -- results from a deficient production of insulin by the pancreas or by ineffectiveness of the insulin produced.

Approximately one in every five people affected by the disease develops the insulin-dependent form of diabetes and becomes totally dependent on daily life-saving insulin injections. Up to 30 per cent of victims may use insulin injections some or all of the time to control their condition.

The price of insulin varies widely from country to country, ranging from less than $3 to $22 a vial, according to WHO. Apart from prohibitive cost to victims in many African states, unreliable supplies and storage difficulties pose problems.
